text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 11: The gain from the extra variables by hour of day'

g.text: Figure 11: The gain from the extra variables by hour of day

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, September 2019 to June 2026. ERA5: ECMWF's reanalysis of past weather. CAMS: satellite irradiance service. Line: the mean absolute error with the first variable set minus the error with the second, as a percentage of the second's error. Band: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Below the dashed line is a gain. Dotted line: between 09 and 10 UTC, where ERA5's cloud fields switch to the next assimilation window (the span of observations that fixes them). A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given. G0: sun position, ERA5 solar radiation (ssrd), and air temperature (t2m). Each group adds to the one before. G1: total cloud cover. G2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. G3: clear-sky radiation. G4: cloud water and cloud base height. G5: direct beam. G6: wind and thermal radiation. G7: humidity and haze. G8: snow and albedo. G9 (the full set): all other ERA5 variables. G10: G9 plus CAMS aerosol. Clearness index: irradiance divided by the irradiance at the top of the atmosphere. An hour with too few months for an interval is not drawn. Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.'
text.tspan: Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, September 2019 to June 2026. ERA5: ECMWF's reanalysis of past weather. CAMS:
Line: the mean absolute error with the first variable set minus the error with
the second, as a percentage of the second's error. Band: 95% interval from
resampling whole months. Below the dashed line is a gain.
Dotted line: between 09 and 10 UTC, where ERA5's cloud fields switch to the next
assimilation window (the span of observations that fixes them).
A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given. G0: sun position, ERA5 solar
radiation (ssrd), and air temperature (t2m). Each group adds to the one before.
G1: total cloud cover. G2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. G3: clear-sky radiation.
G4: cloud water and cloud base height. G5: direct beam. G6: wind and thermal radiation.
G7: humidity and haze. G8: snow and albedo. G9 (the full set): all other ERA5 variables.
Clearness index: irradiance divided by the irradiance at the top of the atmosphere.
An hour with too few months for an interval is not drawn.
Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.
